openItems: Stop condition 2 triggered: AC-1 resolves to (b), not (a) or (c). This is a design/authorization decision for the PO, not a documentation fix: whether to (i) commission an actual independent privacy re-review that either grants D-1's three files a scoped exemption from rule 11 and re-binds privacy-review.md's S5 PASS to the current candidate (which also closes sibling finding F2), or (ii) decide the files require remediation (relocation/rework) despite being functionally privacy-conservative.

Finding F2 (backlog/items/2026-08-31-the-privacy-sign-off-is-bound-to-a-superseded-candidate.md) is directly entangled with this decision: privacy-review.md's S5 PASS predates D-1 entirely, so no valid privacy pass covers the current candidate at all. Recommend resolving F1 and F2 together in one privacy-review pass rather than piecemeal -- fixing rule 11's text alone, without re-binding the PASS, would leave the document internally inconsistent in a different way.

The backlog item's own Proposal section and the prior Elephant/PO dispositions (2026-08-31) considered only 'amend spec.md's inventory' or 'relocate the files' as fix routes -- both touch the digest-bound spec.md/lifecycle.json. Neither considered that the true finding might be an authorization gap. This briefing's own instruction not to inherit the item's lean without checking is what surfaced the difference; the Elephant should update the item's own Triage to reflect it (out of scope for me -- 'do not close or edit any backlog item').
